Model 4 ﬁtted the data well: a non-signiﬁcant χ2 was obtained (52.55; df=49; p=.34), all ﬁt indexes exceeded .90, and the
RMSEA was signiﬁcant (p<.05). However, two direct relations proved not signiﬁcant: the relation between anxiety and leadership
experiences (β=−.08, p<.05) and the relation between secure attachment and leadership experiences (β=.21, p=.07). Still, the
ﬁt of this alternative model indicates that anxiety is negatively and signiﬁcantly related to secure attachment style.
To test whether openness to experience may be the main independent variable predicting attachment and anxiety we tested
another alternative, model 5, presented in Fig. 6.
Model 5 did not ﬁt the data as well as model 4: a signiﬁcant χ2 was obtained (113.5; df=49; p=.00), some ﬁt indexes did not
exceed .90, and the RMSEA was not signiﬁcant (p<.05). The relationship between trait anxiety and leadership experiences (β=−.11,
p<.05), as well as that between attachment and leadership experiences (β=.17, p=.06), were not signiﬁcant.

Greater value from earning money for others?
I tested whether participants simply placed a higher value on
having their friends beneﬁt than they did on having themselves
beneﬁt. To account for this possibility, participants indicated on a
seven-point Likert scale whether they would prefer to (1) have a
friend receive a dollar per word jumble they solved or (7) receive
an additional dollar themselves. One-sample t-tests relative to
scale midpoints of four revealed that participants would rather re-
ceive an additional dollar themselves than have a friend receive
that dollar (M = 5.19, SD = 2.22), t(254) = 8.55, p < .001.
Post-hoc analysis of gender effects
Numerous researchers have posited that men and women take
different approaches to ethical reasoning and are therefore differ-
entially likely to exhibit competitive behavior (Croson & Gneezy,
2009) and to behave unethically (Barnett & Karson, 1987; Dobson
& White, 1995; Gilligan, 1982; O’Fallon & Butterﬁeld, 2005;
Vermeir & Van Kenhove, 2008). These researchers hold that while
men are primarily concerned with an ethic of justice, women are
more concerned with an ethic of care (Gilligan, 1982; Gilligan,

Toronto-alexithymia scale (TAS-20)
The TAS-20 is the most widely used measure of the alexithymia construct (Bagby, Parker,
& Taylor, 1994; Bagby, Taylor, & Parker, 1994). It is comprised of 20 items that are rated
